digest.en: Flávio Bolsonaro’s surge in Brazil’s election threatens climate policy, while a Russian strike kills 18 in Pryluky. Kenya races to trace contacts after its first Ebola death. The Black Sea sees a tanker hit by naval drones near Sochi.
digest.hi: भारत और इटली ने नई दिल्ली में आतंकवाद और संगठित अपराध के खिलाफ सहयोग बढ़ाने के लिए संयुक्त कार्य समूह की बैठक की। इसी दौरान सऊदी अरब में हूती विद्रोहियों ने तेल टैंकों और होर्मुज वैकल्पिक मार्ग पर कई हमले किए, जिससे क्षेत्रीय सुरक्षा पर दबाव बढ़ा।

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro’s advance in Brazil’s election is grim jolt for climate campaigners
articles.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro’s election lead threatens Amazon conservation efforts. Climate campaigners warn of increased deforestation and ecosystem collapse. President Lula’s success in curbing deforestation failed to translate into electoral support. The rainforest faces a critical four-year period. Inquest under way into why President Lula’s success in curbing Amazon deforestation has not lead to success at pollsMore fire, more ash, more crime, more death.

articles.title: Nepal moves to amend laws to facilitate death registration of 5,285 still missing after August 26
articles.summary: Nepal is amending disaster and identity laws to register the deaths of 5,285 people missing since the August 26 earthquake. The changes aim to resolve legal hurdles families face when proving their relatives are dead. The government is preparing amendments to the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act and the National Identity Card and Registration Act to address difficulties faced by families of missing people in registering their deaths, officials said.

articles.title: Israel strikes Gaza on October 7 anniversary, three dead: officials
articles.summary: Israeli forces struck Gaza on the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks, killing three people. Loud explosions were heard near the Nova festival site where families gathered to mourn the 300 victims killed three years ago. Loud bangs across the border in Gaza were audible from the site of the Nova music festival just as family members gathered at dawn to mourn the more than 300 revellers killed three years earlier.

articles.title: Sanctioned Belarus Trucks And A Mystery Logo: 'HAL' Vehicles Spotted In Minsk
articles.summary: Trucks bearing the unknown "HAL" logo have appeared in Minsk. The vehicles likely originate from the sanctioned Minsk Automobile Plant, reflecting deepening trade ties between Belarus and Indonesia despite Western restrictions on the manufacturer. Belarus’s Minsk Automobile Plant is under Western sanctions, limiting who can buy the vehicles produced there. That may be the reason trucks branded with the previously unknown “HAL” badge have been spotted amid strengthening trade relations between Belarus and Indonesia.

articles.title: Fears grow as Flávio Bolsonaro vows to ‘re-democratise’ Brazil
articles.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro vowed to re-democratise Brazil after winning the first round. Critics fear he will continue his father’s authoritarian rule. The son of the disgraced ex-president leads the race. His victory signals the rapid rise of the Bolsonaro political house. After a surprise first-round victory, critics suggest son of disgraced ex-president could seek to continue his father’s authoritarian ruleFlávio’s surprise first-round win highlights rapid rise of Brazil’s House of BolsonaroFlávio Bolsonaro, the far-right frontrunner to become Brazil’s next president, has vowed to “re-democratise” the South American country, fuelling fears over a move into authori.

articles.title: Reopening Brexit debate a ‘terrible idea’: Conservative leader Badenoch
articles.summary: Kemi Badenoch called reopening the Brexit debate a terrible idea. She argued the process wasted years on circular arguments with the European Union. The Conservative leader said the time lost arguing with themselves and Brussels was unacceptable. “Can you imagine having to go through that again?

articles.title: Why the Mecca Agreement Might Fail
articles.summary: The Mecca Agreement faces structural weakness if members maintain separate partnerships while expecting others to absorb their security risks. The mutual defense clause becomes ambiguous when a crisis forces nations to prioritize their own alliances. If each member preserves its own partnerships while expecting the others to absorb its security risks, what does the promise that an attack against one is an attack against all mean when a crisis arrives?

articles.title: Kenya races to trace all contacts after first Ebola death, WHO official says
articles.summary: Kenya is tracing all contacts of its first Ebola death case. The World Health Organization’s top official in the country confirmed that the United Nations and partners are providing full support for the rapid response effort. Kenya’s first Ebola death has triggered a race to trace everyone the victim came into contact with, as the United Nations and partners provide full support, the World Health Organization’s (WHO) top official in the country has told UN News in her first interview on the case.

articles.title: Massive Russian Attack Kills At Least 18, Devastates Pryluky Apartment Block
articles.summary: Russia launched a massive overnight missile and drone attack on Ukraine. At least 19 people died in the strikes. A five-story apartment block in Pryluky was severely damaged. Homes and infrastructure in Kremenchuk also suffered extensive destruction. Russia launched a massive overnight missile and drone attack across Ukraine, killing at least 19 people. Strikes severely damaged a 5-story apartment building in the northeastern city of Pryluky and caused extensive damage to homes and infrastructure in Kremenchuk in the central Poltava region.

articles.title: Oil Tanker Hit By Naval Drones Near Sochi, Sparking Massive Fire On Black Sea
articles.summary: A Liberian-flagged tanker caught fire off Sochi after a drone attack on October 6. All 23 Indian crew members were rescued. Ukrainian monitors identified the vessel as part of Russia’s shadow fleet. The incident highlights growing risks to commercial shipping in the Black Sea. A Liberian-flagged oil tanker caught fire off the Russian resort city of Sochi after an apparent drone attack, Russian authorities said on October 6.

articles.title: US-Australia hypersonic push no silver bullet against China
articles.summary: The US and Australia conducted an inaugural hypersonic weapon flight test over an Australian range. The exercise demonstrates a joint push for standoff strike capabilities. However, the weapon’s combat value depends on whether allied airbases can survive China’s long-range fires. The inaugural flight-test release of a US air-launched hypersonic weapon over an Australian weapons range demonstrates both nations’ push for standoff hypersonic strike, yet the weapon’s true combat value hinges on whether allied airbases and kill chains can survive China’s long-range fires.

articles.title: When Asia’s central banks turn bond vigilante on Trump
articles.summary: Asian central banks may stop buying US Treasuries due to Trump's trade policies. Japan and China have historically been major creditors. Their potential withdrawal would strain Washington's debt financing. Geopolitical tensions are forcing a reassessment of long-standing financial commitments. TOKYO – For decades, the US enjoyed a remarkable luxury: its two biggest creditors, Japan and China, kept showing up at Treasury auctions with checkbooks open.

articles.title: How China deploys wartime history against Japan
articles.summary: Xi Jinping used his Washington visit to undermine US-Japan relations. He deployed wartime history to challenge Tokyo's security posture. Japanese leaders arranged a brief UN meeting to counter this. The strategic goal was to weaken the American alliance with Japan. Beyond all the pageantry, the Chinese leader Xi Jinping had a strategic goal for his Washington visit – to undermine the American relationship with Japan.

articles.title: US man arrested as second suspect in Canada mass school shooting planned with ChatGPT
articles.summary: The US Department of Justice detained James Codey Bryant as a second suspect in a Canadian school shooting. Prosecutors allege he provided technical advice to the primary suspect. The incident involved an eighteen-year-old who allegedly killed six children after discussing the plan with ChatGPT. Justice department detained James Codey Bryant and allege he offered ‘technical advice’ to primary suspectA surprise suspected accomplice has been arrested in connection with a mass school shooting in Canada that was made notorious after an 18-year-old allegedly killed six children after discussing it with the AI chatbot ChatGPT. The US Department of Justice said Tuesday it had detained James Codey.

articles.title: A Lawmaker's Claim That 'Ukraine Is Losing' And Should Consider Compromise Sparks Debate
articles.summary: Ukrainian lawmaker Oleksiy Honcharenko suggested Kyiv is losing the war. He urged the country to consider compromises with Moscow. His opposition party ejected him from its parliamentary faction. The remarks intensified internal debate. A prominent lawmaker has sparked controversy by saying Ukraine is losing the war and should consider making controversial compromises with Moscow. An opposition party ejected Oleksiy Honcharenko from its parliamentary faction, but his remarks may fuel further debate amid relentless Russian attacks.

articles.title: Kenya confirms first Ebola case as virus ‘surges’ in DR Congo province
articles.summary: Kenya confirmed its first Ebola death after a citizen arrived from the DRC. Health officials identified twenty-eight close contacts for monitoring. The virus continues to spread rapidly in the DRC's north-east. This marks the seventeenth known outbreak of the disease in the region. Health minister says 28 contacts identified after death of citizen who arrived from DRC on SaturdayKenya has reported its first-ever Ebola death, the health minister announced on Tuesday, as the disease continues to spread rapidly through the north-east of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where the outbreak was announced in May. This is the 17th outbreak of the highly infectious, often deadl.

articles.title: Testing and monitoring underway in suspected Russia plague death
articles.summary: The World Health Organization confirmed testing for a suspected plague case in Siberia. A laboratory worker died in the region. The agency stated it is monitoring the situation closely. The death of a lab worker in Russia’s Siberia region has sparked concerns over a possible plague case, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday, adding that it was following the situation closely.

articles.title: From drought to deluge: ‘Super’ El Niño’s expanding reach
articles.summary: Papua New Guinea faces drying water sources and failing crops. Food prices are rising months before peak agricultural damage. Pacific Ocean temperatures have surpassed records from 1997 and 2015. Experts are labeling this pattern a Super El Niño. Across Papua New Guinea, water sources are drying up, crops are failing and food prices are rising months before the worst agricultural impacts are expected.

articles.title: When streets become pharmacies: Booming illicit markets in Central Africa
articles.summary: Central Africa seized over 250 tonnes of illicit medical products in six years. The black market thrives due to fragile local health systems. Antibiotics, malaria treatments, and opioids circulate freely on the streets. This undermines public health efforts and regulatory oversight in the region. Antibiotics, malaria treatments, painkillers, opioids. More than 250 tonnes of medical products were seized over six years in Central Africa.

articles.title: Death At Russian Plague Lab: How Much Should We Worry?
articles.summary: A Russian laboratory technician died from suspected pneumonic plague. The incident raised global concerns about potential wider transmission. Experts assessed the risk and Russia's containment response. The case highlights vulnerabilities in handling highly infectious pathogens. A suspected case of pneumonic plague killing a laboratory technician in Russia has sparked global alarm about the possibility of wider transmission. RFE/RL spoke to Brendan Wren, a professor of microbial pathogenesis, about the situation and Russia's moves to deal with it.

articles.title: CPEC 2.0 will be won or lost on keeping China’s investors safe
articles.summary: CPEC 2.0 shifts focus from fixed infrastructure to industry, agriculture, and private business. This transition complicates security for Chinese investors in Pakistan. Protecting dispersed industrial zones and mines requires different strategies than guarding large, static construction sites. CPEC 2.0 aims to move past the infrastructure-heavy first phase toward industry, agriculture, mining, technology, green development and business-to-business investment. That shift could deepen economic ties between Pakistan and China, but it also changes the nature of the security challenge.

articles.title: Tigray rebel groups ‘forcibly recruiting boys as young as 15’ as fighting spreads
articles.summary: A new Tigray rebel alliance is forcibly recruiting boys as young as fifteen. Fighting resumed on 23 September, threatening a fresh humanitarian crisis in northern Ethiopia. Civilians are fleeing as armed groups round up men and boys on the streets. Civilians try to flee as men and boys rounded up on streets by new alliance as Ethiopia conflict erupts againAs renewed fighting has threatened a fresh humanitarian crisis in the northern region of Ethiopia, reports are emerging that a new alliance of armed groups in Tigray has been forcibly recruiting men and boys to its ranks. Renewed conflict erupted on 23 September between Ethiopia’s federal go.

articles.title: Sustaining Northeast Asia trilateral deterrence
articles.summary: US, South Korean, and Japanese planners have institutionalized trilateral security cooperation. However, deterrence credibility depends on wartime sustainment capabilities. The three nations have expanded joint exercises to address this critical operational variable. Originally published by Pacific Forum, this article is republished with permission. While operational planners in the United States, the Republic of Korea and Japan have made historic strides institutionalizing trilateral security cooperation, the credibility of deterrence ultimately hinges on a more punishing variable: wartime sustainment.

articles.title: Guardian readers fund life-changing surgery for Somali boy injured in US airstrike
articles.summary: Guardian readers funded life-saving surgery for Abdiqadir Salah, a seven-year-old Somali boy injured in a US drone strike. The operation took place in Mogadishu after an investigation revealed the attack killed twelve civilians. The boy’s mother described the hospital journey as a moment of mixed joy and apprehension. After Guardian investigation uncovered drone strike that killed 12 civilians and injured many more, seven-year-old Abdiqadir Salah underwent vital operation in MogadishuOn the rickshaw ride to the hospital, Marian Haji Abdi Guled felt a mixture of joy and apprehension: the day they had been waiting for had finally arrived. Almost a year earlier, her then seven-year-old son, Abdiqadir Salah, had bee.

articles.title: ‘Nothing can justify these atrocities,’ says Guterres three years on from 7 October attacks
articles.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated nothing justifies the atrocities committed on 7 October. Speaking three years after the initial attacks, he called for an end to the suffering of both Israelis and Palestinians in the ongoing conflict. Three years after Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups attacked Israel, UN Secretary-General António Guterres has said nothing can justify the atrocities of 7 October – calling for an end to the suffering of Israelis and Palestinians alike.

articles.title: इज़रायल-हमास युद्ध को 3 साल पूरे, गाज़ा पर हमले में मारे गए 5 फिलिस्तीनी
articles.summary: इज़रायल-हमास युद्ध को तीन वर्ष पूरे हुए। इस अवसर पर गाज़ा पर इज़रायली हमलों में चार फिलिस्तीनी मारे गए। इज़रायल-हमास युद्ध (Israel-Hamas War) को आज 3 साल पूरे हो गए हैं। 2023 में आज ही के दिन 7 अक्टूबर को फिलिस्तीनी आतंकी संगठन हमास ने इज़रायल पर करीब 5,000 रॉकेट्स दागते हुए और म्यूज़िक फेस्टिवल में कत्लेआम मचाते हुए जंग की शुरुआत की थी, जिसके बाद इज़रायल ने भी गाज़ा और आसपास के फिलिस्तीनी इलाकों में सैन्य कार्रवाई शुरू कर दी, जो अभी भी जारी है।

articles.summary: रूस के साइबेरिया में एक शोध केंद्र पर प्लेग नमूने के टूटने से 28 वर्षीय वैज्ञानिक की मौत हुई। दूसरा कर्मचारी भी बीमार पड़ा है। लगभग 200 लोगों को क्वारंटाइन किया गया। विश्व स्वास्थ्य संगठन ने रूस से स्पष्टीकरण मांगा है। रूस के साइबेरिया की एक रिसर्च लैब में 28 साल की महिला वैज्ञानिक की रहस्यमयी निमोनिया से मौत हो गई है.

articles.summary: ईरानी राष्ट्रपति मसूद पेजेशकियन ने अमेरिका के साथ संतुलित शांति समझौते के लिए तैयारी जताई। उन्होंने कहा कि यह समझौता क्षेत्रीय सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करेगा। हालांकि, ईरान अपने राष्ट्रीय हितों और नागरिक अधिकारों से समझौता नहीं करेगा। US Iran conflict: ईरान ने अमेरिका से शांति समझौते को लेकर बड़ा संकेत दिया है। ईरानी राष्ट्रपति मसूद पेजेशकियन ने कहा है कि उनका देश ऐसा समझौता करने के लिए तैयार है, जो संतुलित और निष्पक्ष हो और क्षेत्र में लंबे समय तक शांति और सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित कर सके।

articles.title: अमेरिका के ‘गद्दार मेजर’ को कुर्सी से बांधकर छाती पर मारी जाएगी गोली, 81 साल में पहली बार आर्मी
articles.summary: फोर्ट हुड में 13 सैनिकों की हत्या के आरोपी पूर्व मेजर निदाल हसन को मौत की सजा मिली। राष्ट्रपति ट्रंप ने डेथ वारंट पर हस्ताक्षर किए। 3 दिसंबर 2026 को उन्हें फायरिंग स्क्वाड द्वारा फांसी दी जाएगी। यह 81 वर्षों में पहली ऐसी सजा है। अमेरिका के फोर्ट हुड सैन्य अड्डे पर 13 निहत्थे सैनिकों की हत्या करने वाले पूर्व मेजर निदाल हसन को अब सजा-ए-मौत दी जाएगी.

articles.title: बजरंग बली का भक्त है चीनी बच्चा! हनुमान चालीसा सुनकर ही आती है नींद, मां भी हैरान- ये क्या कनेक्शन
articles.summary: चार माह के चीनी शिशु को हनुमान चालीसा सुनाने पर चिड़चिड़ापन शांत हो जाता है। माता का कहना है कि यह ध्वनि उसे तुरंत सुला देती है। तभी तो ये एक छोटे से बच्चे को भी शब्दों से भले ही नहीं लेकिन भावना से ऐसी समझ में आई कि वो इसे सुनते ही कितना भी चिड़चिड़ा हो, शांत होकर सोने लगता है.
